Create one independently chosen complex documentary street-photo test scene, using the supplied portrait only for visible adult appearance guidance, then test whether its specified visual components appear in generated pixels.

A candid, photorealistic street photograph of one adult woman whose visible adult facial features and long, dark, loosely wavy hair are guided by the attached portrait. She stands on a pedestrian bridge just after a shower, with the bridge railing close beside her and the walkway receding into softer distance. Caught in the same instant, her left hand raises the straight shaft of an open transparent umbrella from beside her left shoulder until the canopy clears her head; her right hand holds a small printed route card at chest height, turned toward her eyes. Her face stays visible in three-quarter view as she reads the card, brows gently focused. Wind from camera-right pushes loose hair toward camera-left and tips the canopy slightly toward its source, while her planted feet and quiet weight shift keep her balanced. Fresh droplets cling to the clear canopy and sleeve, and a single shallow puddle near her shoes reflects a small patch of pale sky. The foreground railing has crisp wet texture, the far bridge fades naturally, and soft overcast daylight gives skin, fabric, acrylic, and concrete distinct believable surfaces. Frame this at casual phone height with ordinary observational timing and natural scale.

obligation.composition_instruction: Preserve the requested adult fictional identity, role, wardrobe, and visual style. In one still, keep a calm low-expression baseline visibly stable while one concrete, quiet practical action helps one identifiable trusted adult counterpart and leaves an already-visible helpful consequence for that same counterpart. Add only one localized warmth leak, such as slight lower-lid easing, a restrained brow release, a fractional mouth-corner softening, or reduced tension in the hand or shoulder nearest the target. Optional outward support may use economical gesture, stable upright posture, a neat simple silhouette, restrained grooming, or a muted/cool-neutral palette, but these are conventions rather than requirements. Do not assign fixed hair color, eye color, hairstyle, costume, gender, occupation, gaze direction, camera angle, or prop, and do not let expressionlessness, competence, beauty, a cool palette, or a caring object substitute for the same-target action and consequence. Preserve the counterpart's autonomy; avoid hostile denial, shy withdrawal, possessive control, broad open affection, or an abrupt personality switch.

render_gates.description: Lens, sensor, exposure, and image surface read as clean photographic capture rather than a damaged display or file.
The scene establishes an immediately familiar and physically coherent baseline before the contradiction is inspected.
Exactly one spatial, temporal, causal, optical, or topological invariant supplies the governing error rule.
At least three affected surfaces repeat the same measurable displacement, lag, dependency, correspondence, or recursion.

Within every affected region, native material identity, local texture, lighting, thickness, depth, boundary shape, and occlusion remain coherent under the shared rule; source pixels or facial texture are not stamped onto unrelated surfaces.
Unaffected anatomy, objects, perspective, lighting, and materials remain internally coherent and physically plausible.

The contradiction appears at the deliberately selected reveal strength, immediate or delayed, while remaining clearly authored, subordinate to one inferable world rule, and distinguishable from generic image failure.

A screen effect, split seam, collage, visible translucent shell, enclosing splash ring, portal, magical rift, flat image-plane slice, particle dissolve, or random anomaly stack does not substitute for the repeated world rule.

Without prompt text, a caption, or metadata, a viewer can state the single failed world rule and point to at least three separated instances that share its same measurable relation; merely saying that something looks wrong fails.
An isolated malformed hand or face, fused object, broken texture or text, accidental reflection or shadow mismatch, or other familiar synthesis defect does not carry the reality-error concept.
